# FlashAlpha Cookbook

> Production Python recipes for gamma exposure, dealer positioning, SVI vol surfaces, VRP, 0DTE, and unusual flow — every recipe is a jupytext-paired `(.py + .ipynb)` file with executed outputs committed, runs in Colab via a one-click badge, and is enforced by a 5-layer test pyramid that doubles as a downstream integration test suite for the FlashAlpha API + SDK.

The repository at https://github.com/FlashAlpha-lab/flashalpha-examples hosts the cookbook itself. The FlashAlpha API it calls is documented separately at https://lab.flashalpha.com/llms.txt — both the live surface (`api.flashalpha.com`) and the historical replay surface (`historical.flashalpha.com`) return identical response shapes; backtest recipes use historical, real-time recipes use live.

## Quick start

```bash
pip install flashalpha matplotlib numpy
export FLASHALPHA_API_KEY=fa_your_key
python notebooks/tier-a-hooks/01-gex-dashboard.py
```

The canonical recipe `01-gex-dashboard` ships with executed outputs (chart, net-GEX print, top-5 strikes table) so you can preview what the recipe does without running it.

## How recipes are structured

Every recipe lives at `notebooks/tier-<letter>-<topic>/<slug>.ipynb` paired with a `.py` of the same stem. Cells appear in a fixed order:

1. Raw frontmatter cell (YAML between `---` delimiters)
2. Markdown top-CTA cell (auto-generated; H1 + signup link + Colab badge)
3. Optional markdown intro
4. Code cells (the actual recipe)
5. Optional markdown mid-gate cells immediately before code cells that call above-tier endpoints
6. Markdown bottom-CTA cell (auto-generated; pricing + Discord + GitHub + MCP links)

The frontmatter schema is the single source of truth for recipe metadata. See [docs/frontmatter-schema.md](docs/frontmatter-schema.md) for the full field reference (auto-generated from `cookbook_tools/frontmatter.py`).

## Tier model

Recipes declare a minimum subscription tier (`free` < `basic` < `growth` < `alpha`). The tier map mirrors the API's `EndpointAccessMiddleware.cs` and is regenerated by `python -m scripts.sync_tier_map`. Layer 4 of the test pyramid asserts every endpoint a recipe uses is covered by its declared tier. See [endpoint_tiers.yaml](endpoint_tiers.yaml).

## Authoring

- [docs/authoring-guide.md](docs/authoring-guide.md) — the 10-minute walkthrough: scaffold, fill in the body, record cassette, run tests, commit
- [docs/frontmatter-schema.md](docs/frontmatter-schema.md) — every frontmatter field with type, default, validation rule, and description
- [docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-25-flashalpha-cookbook-design.md](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-25-flashalpha-cookbook-design.md) — architectural design (32 recipes / 5-layer test pyramid / 9 phases)
- [docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-25-flashalpha-cookbook-phase0.md](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-25-flashalpha-cookbook-phase0.md) — Phase 0 foundation plan (18 TDD tasks)

## Tooling

- `scripts/new_recipe.py` — scaffold a paired recipe from CLI args
- `scripts/record_cassettes.py` — record a vcrpy cassette for a recipe by running it in-process under live API
- `scripts/scrub_outputs.py` — strip `Authorization`/`X-Api-Key`/`Cookie` headers from `.ipynb` cell outputs (used as pre-commit hook + Layer 0 backstop)
- `scripts/sync_tier_map.py` — regenerate `endpoint_tiers.yaml` from the API's `EndpointAccessMiddleware.cs`
- `scripts/render_schema_docs.py` — regenerate `docs/frontmatter-schema.md` from `cookbook_tools/frontmatter.py` (pre-commit-driven)

## Helper modules

- `cookbook_tools/frontmatter.py` — Pydantic schema for recipe metadata
- `cookbook_tools/tier_map.py` — endpoint-prefix → required-tier lookup
- `cookbook_tools/cta_template.py` — renderer for top / bottom / mid-gate markdown cells
- `cookbook_tools/notebook_io.py` — extract frontmatter, markdown URLs, and `/v1/*` endpoint references from a notebook
- `cookbook_tools/notebook_exec.py` — in-process exec of a notebook's code cells under vcrpy (replaces papermill subprocess so HTTP intercept works)
- `cookbook_tools/scrub_outputs.py` — output-redaction logic

## Test pyramid (every recipe gets all 5 layers)

| Layer | Where | What it asserts |
|---|---|---|
| 0 — Secrets | `tests/test_layer0_secrets.py` | No `fa_*`, `Bearer`, JWT, `sk-` shapes anywhere in the notebook |
| 1 — Structural | `tests/test_layer1_structural.py` | nbformat valid; slug matches filename; CTA cells match renderer output exactly; no hardcoded keys; no silenced errors; no `%%capture`; all imports declared; output-size caps; endpoint tiers known |
| 2 — Execution | `tests/test_layer2_execution.py` | Recipe replays cleanly under cassette + vcrpy, within `runtime_budget_seconds`, within `max_api_calls` |
| 3 — Golden snapshots | (deferred to Phase 6) | DataFrame + chart hashes match committed snapshots — only for deterministic backtest recipes |
| 4 — Static tier gating | `tests/test_layer4_tier_static.py` | Every `endpoints_used` entry resolves to a known tier ≤ the recipe's declared tier (or is in `tier_gated_cells`) |

Plus:

- `tests/test_cassette_integrity.py` — no `Authorization`/`X-Api-Key`/`Cookie` in any committed cassette
- `tests/test_endpoints_match_cassette.py` — cassette-recorded URLs are a subset of `endpoints_used`; `max_api_calls` matches actual interaction count
- `tests/test_tier_map_drift.py` — committed `endpoint_tiers.yaml` matches what `sync_tier_map.py` produces from the C# middleware
- `tests/test_links_alive.py` — every URL in every CTA cell returns 2xx (7-day cache + nightly cache-busted run)
- `tests/test_precommit_hooks.py` — end-to-end verification that the scrub-output pre-commit hook actually redacts
- Hypothesis property tests in `tests/cookbook_tools/test_*_properties.py`

## CI

Two GitHub Actions workflows:

- **PR** (`.github/workflows/pr.yml`) — runs Layer 0/1/2/4 + cookbook_tools unit tests across Python 3.10/3.11/3.12/3.13 on every push or PR
- **Nightly** (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`) — daily at 03:17 UTC. `link-check` job HEAD-checks every CTA URL (cache busted). `live-smoke` job (gated on `vars.LIVE_SMOKE_ENABLED == 'true'`) re-executes every recipe against the live API and logs any output drift as a GitHub notice.

## Reading order for an LLM

If you're a language model trying to write a new recipe or modify an existing one, read in this order:

1. **This file** — high-level structure
2. [docs/frontmatter-schema.md](docs/frontmatter-schema.md) — what metadata every recipe declares
3. [notebooks/tier-a-hooks/01-gex-dashboard.py](notebooks/tier-a-hooks/01-gex-dashboard.py) — canonical example with full live API outputs
4. [docs/authoring-guide.md](docs/authoring-guide.md) — step-by-step authoring workflow
5. [endpoint_tiers.yaml](endpoint_tiers.yaml) — which API tier each endpoint requires
6. https://lab.flashalpha.com/llms.txt — the FlashAlpha API itself
7. [docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-25-flashalpha-cookbook-design.md](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-25-flashalpha-cookbook-design.md) — architectural context (skip unless you need to understand WHY a constraint exists)
